Acknowledgement of Country

The Victorian Curriculum and Assessment Authority proudly acknowledges and pays respect to Victoria’s Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and their rich and enduring cultures.

We acknowledge Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people as Australia’s first peoples and as the Traditional Owners and custodians of the lands and waters on which we rely. We pay respect to Elders past and present of the lands where we conduct our work and recognise their ongoing contributions as the first educators on the land now known as Victoria.

Watch now: To find out more about the Arts Foundation to Level 6, watch ‘Understanding the Victorian Curriculum F–10 Version 2.0, The Arts Foundation to Level 6’ on the About the Arts page. To find out more about Media Arts Levels 7–10, watch ‘Understanding the Victorian Curriculum F–10 Version 2.0, Media Arts Levels 7–10’ on the Resources page.

Rationale and Aims

Rationale

In Media Arts, communication, storytelling and persuasion are used to connect audiences, purposes and ideas. Media Arts explores concepts and perspectives, and examines, interprets and analyses media practices that represent the world from diverse perspectives. Media artists work collaboratively and use traditional and emerging media technologies and creative processes to plan, produce and distribute media arts works.

Through the creative use of materials and technologies to convey meaning, students create and manipulate still and moving images, text, sound and interactive elements. They construct representations and communicate or challenge understandings, ideas and positions.

Media arts plays an important role in sustaining cultural diversity and continuing local, national and global cultures, particularly the cultures of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples. It offers opportunities to use media platforms to celebrate, maintain or revitalise ways of knowing, being, doing, belonging and becoming. Through media arts, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples celebrate and express connection to and responsibility for Country and Place.

The Media Arts curriculum recognises that media forms can operate at either a mass level or at an interpersonal level, where communication occurs between individuals and among online communities. Students critically reflect on the role of media in society and consider how their own media engagement is shaped by the practices of media. They develop awareness and understanding of ways that media institutions use information collected from users to create communities and to mediate users’ media choices.

Students learn to be critically aware of the ways that media is used culturally, how it might be negotiated by different audiences and the impact it can have on their own understanding of the world.

Aims

The Media Arts curriculum aims to develop students’:

  • enjoyment and confidence to participate in, experiment with and interpret the media-rich culture and communications practices that surround them
  • creative and critical thinking skills through engagement as producers and consumers of media
  • aesthetic knowledge and sense of curiosity and discovery as they explore images, text and sound to express ideas, concepts and stories for different audiences
  • knowledge and understanding of their active participation in existing and evolving local, national and global media cultures.

Structure

The Media Arts curriculum is presented as one curriculum level at Foundation and then in 2-level bands from Levels 1 to 10.

Foundation Levels A to D for the Arts bring together learning from Dance, Drama, Media Arts, Music and Visual Arts. Foundation Levels A to D curriculum levels are developed for students with intellectual disability and learning delay.

Media Arts comprises 4 interrelated strands:

  • Exploring
  • Developing Practices
  • Creating
  • Presenting.

Exploring

In this strand, students learn as artists and as audiences. They explore:

  • media arts works and media contexts in the lives of individuals and groups across cultures, times, places and other contexts
  • the diversity of how, where and why people create, make, distribute and respond to media arts works
  • the diversity and significance of media arts for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, cultures and communities
  • how media arts works communicate cultural and aesthetic knowledge, purpose, meaning and emotion
  • how media arts develops empathy and understanding of multiple perspectives and viewpoints.

Students respond using media arts practices and forms, images, sounds, movement, language and/or digital tools.

Developing Practices

In this strand, students develop practices and skills for producing and responding to media arts. Students develop skills through experimentation and creative and critical thinking. They develop creative and critical practices, including:

  • creative skills and confidence to imagine, use and manipulate visual and aural elements, media languages and technologies to create representations that communicate stories, narratives, ideas and meaning
  • safe and ethical use of production processes using available resources
  • critical skills in observing, reflecting, analysing and evaluating their own and others’ media arts practices, using language/terminology and embodied practices.

Creating

In this strand, as artists, students apply media arts and production processes. As audiences, they reflect on their work as it develops, for example through observation, analysis, reflection, evaluation and considering the relationships their work creates with audiences.

Students use media arts concepts and production processes to construct representations and produce media arts works in a range of forms, styles and/or genres.

Presenting

In this strand, students share (exhibit, screen, publish or distribute) their media arts works using spaces and resources. Students may also work collaboratively to produce media arts works. Students:

  • plan and design their presentations, considering audiences and institutional practices
  • share their work using materials and technologies
  • observe and, as appropriate, engage and participate in interactions with media arts works and audiences.

Achievement standards

Achievement standards describe what students are typically able to understand and do, and they are the basis for reporting student achievement.

Foundation Levels A to D for the Arts provide a developmental continuum with the first achievement standard at Foundation Level A, and then at Foundation Level B, Foundation Level C and Foundation Level D.

From Foundation in Media Arts, students progress along a learning continuum that provides the first achievement standard at Foundation, and then at Levels 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10.

Content descriptions

In Media Arts, content descriptions sequence and describe the knowledge, understanding and skills that teachers need to teach and students are expected to learn.

Elaborations

Elaborations are examples that provide guidance on how the curriculum may be transformed into a classroom activity or learning opportunity. They are provided as advisory material only.

Learning in Media Arts

Media arts practices

In Media Arts, students engage with technologies and interdisciplinary art forms to design, produce, distribute and interact with a range of print, audio, screen-based or hybrid artworks. Students explore, view, analyse and participate in media culture from a range of perspectives and in a variety of contexts. They acquire the knowledge and skills to work in a range of media forms and styles. Students learn to reflect critically on their own and others’ media arts experiences and evaluate media arts works from different cultures, times, places and other contexts including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures. They express, conceptualise and communicate through their media arts works using creative and critical use of language and technologies with increasing complexity and aesthetic understanding.

Media arts concepts

There are 7 concepts fundamental to media arts. They are:

  • media technologies
  • representations
  • audiences
  • institutions
  • media languages
  • viewpoints
  • contexts.

Together, the media arts concepts provide a framework for students to engage with and create media arts works in existing or emerging forms and to consider media arts practices.

The media arts concepts, although discussed independently, are interrelated. Students engage with each of the concepts at varying levels of depth in all levels.

Media technologies

Media technologies are integral to media arts practices. Students:

  • use a range of available digital and analog tools as they create and respond
  • produce media arts works using available and appropriate technology and reflect on the making of their media arts works
  • reflect critically on developments across media technologies and consider responsible and ethical media practices and how media arts are used for diverse purposes across cultures, times, places and other contexts.
Representations

Representations are present in all media arts works. All media arts works are constructed through narratives and media artists build representations of people, places, concepts, themes and events through the stories they tell. Students:

  • examine the construction of representations in narratives in media arts works and build their own
  • reflect critically on the impact of repeated representations and how they change over time and across contexts
  • consider the ways people learn with and from others through viewpoints, values and attitudes embedded in representations in media arts works.
Audiences

All media products are distributed to audiences, who consume them in different ways. Factors such as technology, media literacy and the context of creation and consumption can all alter the way audiences receive, engage with and respond to media products.

All media products are made for target audiences, defined by their cultural, social and historical context, demographics such as age and gender, and individual traits such as values. A media product may be considered successful if the intended audiences receive, engage with and respond to the product the way the media creator intended.

A consideration of audience is a critical aspect of media arts practice. Students:

  • consider the audience(s) that media arts works are made for (target audience), how audiences might interpret the work and differences in interpretations across audiences
  • examine how audiences come together or can be polarised.
Institutions

Media institutions include broadcasting companies; print and digital newspaper and magazine publishers; film, television and screen and music production companies; and other production and publishing companies. Media institutions can be local, national or global and owned or controlled by individuals, corporations or governments. The diversity of media institutions is evolving and dynamic. Students:

  • explore how individuals, communities, organisations and institutions engage in practices that influence media production for economic, political or social gain
  • investigate how media arts works are distributed (shared with audiences)
  • consider their own engagement with media
  • explore responsible media practice, ethical implications of media practices and ways they are influenced by media institutions.
Media languages

Media languages include the still and/or moving images, sounds and texts used to tell a story. Students develop knowledge and use of the language of media in terms of design, production, distribution, consumption, engagement with, reception, reading and critique of their and others’ media products. They also examine the terms used by media practitioners and institutions.

Meaning is created through the use of media codes and media conventions. Media codes and media conventions combine to create a media product and should be seen as working together.

Media codes

Technical, written and symbolic codes have a physical presence in media forms and products and are used to create, construct and suggest meaning. Media codes include camera, lighting, mise en scene, editing, sound, acting, layout, typography, text and images among other things. Codes construct the media form and product.

Media conventions

The elements that create and shape meaning in a media form or product. They include story structure, story principles, genre conventions, character, cause and effect, and point of view. Conventions tend to remain the same across mediums but also refer to the following:

  • Genre conventions: The rules that define genres based on the cultural assumptions about the significance of media products, the type of audiences who consume media products and practices of the media industries.
  • Narrative conventions: Common narrative structures, such as character, character arcs and three-act structures.
Viewpoints

Throughout their Media Arts learning, students use questions based on viewpoints as an inquiry tool for considering their own and others’ use of media arts concepts from multiple perspectives. Students can use questions based on viewpoints to:

  • structure their reasoning and reflecting
  • explore ideas and make decisions
  • explore and develop empathy for multiple perspectives
  • express and celebrate identities, ideas and meaning
  • think deeply about their own media arts practices and media arts works by others that they experience.

As they create and respond to media arts works and experiences, students develop questions to explore ideas, perspectives and meaning. They think and make decisions as artists and as audiences. Questions based on viewpoints encourage students to consider a range of perspectives and to think deeply about their own and others' media arts works.

Contexts

All media arts practices are embedded in the context of the time and place in which they were created and viewed. In Media Arts, students explore and reflect on:

  • the contexts of media forms
  • the ways people learn with and from others through the media
  • their own motivations
  • the relationships they hope to build with audiences
  • the context in which they create media products
  • how online and mobile platforms are developing and the impact this is having on production and distribution practices, and how they construct their relationships with audiences to engage them on platforms
  • the relationships they develop with various media forms as audience.

Media arts forms

Media arts forms refer to the technological means and channels by which the media is created, produced, distributed, consumed and read. Media arts forms can include:

  • moving image, such as film, television, video or animation
  • still image, such as narrative photography
  • audio, such as radio or podcasts
  • print, such as magazines, zines, comics, graphic novels, newspapers or posters
  • digital, such as online video and audio, streaming video and audio, podcasts, magazines, comics, graphic novels, newspapers, video games, blogs, websites or apps
  • convergent or hybridised media, which is the combination or joining of 2 or more media forms, such as photography and animation, print productions and a digital game, or augmented and virtual reality products.

Media production process

There are 5 key stages of the media production process to create media arts works.

Development

Development involves exploring the ideas, intentions, narrative and audience of a production. Students:

  • research other media products, analysing codes and conventions, narrative, genre or style and may consider the context of a product
  • investigate equipment, materials and technologies in a range of media forms relevant to their audience and intention.
Pre-production

Pre-production planning considers the concept, audience, intention, narrative and context of a media product. Pre-production involves planning a narrative, including how it will engage and be consumed and read by an audience. Media codes and conventions, genre and style are considered in the construction of the narrative. Documentation and planning may take visual and written forms, such as production notes or storyboards. Media practitioners may undertake technical tests and experiments prior to production, reflecting on their success or failure.

Production

Production is when a product is captured or recorded. Production may be a collaborative process involving a number of people with specific roles or it may be an individual process. Reflection and evaluation of the production can occur through written documentation, oral feedback and visual feedback.

Post-production

Productions are refined during post-production, considering the intention, audience and planned narrative. Codes and conventions are used to resolve ideas and engage audiences. Specific equipment and technologies are used in editing. Feedback is sought and the creator and audiences reflect on the product, its intent and its relationship to the target audience.

Distribution

The product is delivered to the target audience in a planned context and location.

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Media Arts - Foundation Level A (The Arts FLA-FLD)

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation Level A, the Arts builds on students’ prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for sensory exploration and experiential approaches that enable arts learning experiences across the 5 Arts disciplines: Dance, Drama, Music, Media Arts and Visual Arts. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline.

In Foundation Level A, students explore and develop practices through the Arts disciplines by participating in and interacting with arts experiences, elements, materials and/or technologies.

Learning in the Arts involves exploration together with structured learning opportunities appropriate for the learning needs of individual students.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Foundation Level A, students experience and attend to arts works they encounter at school, home and in the community.

They participate in the co-creation of arts works and contribute to the sharing of arts works with others.

Dance

Students interact with the elements of dance to develop an understanding of movement.

Drama

Students interact with the elements of drama and expressive skills.

Media Arts

Students interact with media arts forms, language and/or technologies.

Music

Students interact with the elements of music and instruments.

Visual Arts

Students interact with art elements and materials.

elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in the use of technologies to capture images or sounds, for example by using a switch or button to activate media equipment to capture an image or to record a sound

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to composition by attending to images and/or sounds when given a choice or having their vocalisations recorded and compiled into a co-created artwork

elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an interest in sounds or the representation of sounds in their environment, for example by attending to a musical sound or vibration by turning their head or body as the sound or sensation travels or by associating music with routines such as musical cues for the start and finish of activities or the school bell

elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in multisensory opportunities to explore music practices such as by listening or feeling, experimenting or playing instruments

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to associate sounds or vibrations with their source, for example by touching a drum in response to a sensation

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the use of art equipment, for example by holding various objects, mark-making tools and materials for short periods of time

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to a visual artwork to explore ideas, for example by reaching towards, touching or exploring objects, environments, colour, texture or materials

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and interacting with two- or three-dimensional artworks that have been created using digital technologies and tools, such as images, soundscapes, interactive artworks, public art or screen-based works

elaborations.name: VC2AFAE01-E25 – The Arts

content_descriptions.name: VC2AFAD01 - The Arts
content_descriptions.text: participate in arts experiences using elements, materials and/or technologies

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E01 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing a performance space, as both a performer and audience member

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the use of props, costumes and sounds as part of play to support movement

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to a range of fundamental movements to music, for example by bending, stretching, twisting, turning (non-locomotor), crawling or moving up and down (locomotor)

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring movement through repeated patterns

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing a reaction to a situation, using their preferred communication modality

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing a performance space, as both a performer and audience member

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring props, costumes, puppets and sounds as part of dramatic play and process drama, for example engaging with and handling props, costumes and puppets or engaging with a puppet using expressive skills such as facial expressions, gestures, movement and/or vocalisations

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and responding to sound in drama such as the sounds of rain and wind, transport or animals

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing media technologies being used to capture images and sounds for stories

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring different ways of using media arts works, for example by taking samples of images or sounds they react to and integrating sounds, images or objects to represent their preference or their responses

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with the use of a digital camera to capture still or moving images, for example by using a switch, clapping to activate and deactivate a camera or viewing or reacting to images created using the effects of a ‘photo booth’ camera application

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the use of software to create a photo story about themselves

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an awareness of a change in elements of music such as duration or dynamics, for example by placing their hand on an instrument that is played softly and then loudly or by turning their head in response to a beat that is slow and then becomes fast

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring instruments by using an instrument, responding to the touch of an instrument or holding and using an instrument with assistance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the accompaniment of chants, songs and/or rhymes using their preferred communication modality or an instrument

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing music for different purposes, for example by using music as a cue for transition, relaxation or movement or to reflect different settings and feelings

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating a preference for art elements such as colour, shape and texture, for example by choosing similar textures, colours or shapes

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in sensory experiences that provide opportunities to explore sights, sounds, smells, tastes and textures and to enjoy and appreciate visual arts materials, techniques and processes, for example by manipulating and exploring the feel of art materials such as clay

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with different materials, techniques and technologies and reacting to the interaction or result

elaborations.name: VC2AFAD01-E25 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with the qualities and properties of materials such as paint, crayons, clay and found objects and showing a preference for or communicating what they would like applied to their visual arts works, for example by showing excitement when paint and a paintbrush or roller is on a table or when an easel is set up with a canvas, ready for painting

content_descriptions.name: VC2AFAC01 - The Arts
content_descriptions.text: contribute to the co-creation of arts works

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E01 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing and responding to concepts through their preferred learning modalities such as visual, kinaesthetic, auditory or tactile

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in sensorimotor experiences, using gentle movements and interactive play to explore different textures and rhythms

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising movements with support to begin to develop technical skills of body control, posture, strength, balance and coordination

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to rhythmic cues or showing an awareness of a movement they have made

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to choose an object to be included in a dance such as a piece of fabric or a prop

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing tactile and sensory stimuli to evoke a sense of place in a drama work, for example by smelling or feeling seaweed, pampas grass or sand or listening to recorded sounds of the sea during a drama work about a seaside location

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the use of props, costumes and sounds to contribute to a performance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding when things that interest them are being used in a dramatic performance, for example smiling when their favourite music is played as part of a performance or reaching out to a favourite prop being used

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a multisensory activity such as exploring sounds, images and text to contribute to a shared media arts work such as an animation or class presentation in response to an event or experience, for example being part of a presentation to their school on a class activity or a response to a story

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: moving shapes or icons on a screen to create a media presentation

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating an artwork after experimenting with images and texts in response to a story about an animal or imaginary creature

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the creation of a presentation in response to a film they have viewed with the class

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to the variety of sounds that can be created with voice and body percussion, for example by listening to, watching or feeling the vibrations of sound effects

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in and attending to the use of sound effects to accompany stories, rhymes, games and pictures, for example participating in choosing and attending to the kinds of sounds that complement these activities

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an object, equipment or instrument to contribute to a group song, for example by activating a switch to play a sound, striking a drum or pressing keys on a musical keyboard

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: showing an interest in experimenting with making sounds using voice and body percussion, for example by imitating interesting sounds made by another, repeating interesting sounds they discover or showing some creativity in using their voice and body to make sounds

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a multisensory activity, exploring materials to contribute to a shared visual artwork in response to an event or experience, for example returning from a community walk and exploring colours, shapes, textures and objects that could contribute to a group artwork and then expressing ideas about what was experienced on the walk (such as crunching leaves, texture of bark and colours)

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: moving objects or images to create an artwork

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a multisensory activity to repurpose materials into a shared artwork based on experimentation, for example using cardboard or objects that create sound and expressing ideas about an imaginary animal or object

elaborations.name: VC2AFAC01-E25 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a visit to an exhibition or art gallery and expressing ideas about the artworks using different materials, sounds or gestures

content_descriptions.name: VC2AFAP01 - The Arts
content_descriptions.text: participate in their arts works being presented

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E01 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing the presentation of their dance in a digital format

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or viewing a recording of their movement or contribution to a dance work (individual and group efforts), for example listening to an audio recording or viewing a video or photograph of their performance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: reacting to an audience when they are performing, for example by changing their expression when they hear or see familiar adults

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing their engagement in a drama work with others in the classroom, for example by interacting with props and puppets or by responding to their teacher in-role

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing a role alongside others, supported by staff in the role, for example by participating in a class or school performance

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: reacting to an audience when they are performing, for example by changing their expression when they hear or see familiar adults

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing the presentation of their drama work in a digital format

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing the sharing of a media arts work that they have contributed to, such as in a digital display in the classroom or school corridor or shared with the class as a reflection and feedback opportunity (such as at a school assembly or on the school website)

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing images that represent an experience or ‘tell a story’

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating a reaction to an event or experience by using sounds and images

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a class presentation of an event or experience around a topic, for example by using sounds, gestures or movement in response to a learning experience, class outing or excursion

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an awareness that others listen to and respond to their voice or sounds

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: having their sound contribution recorded and played back to them and the class

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an awareness of being involved in performing for others, for example by responding to the clapping of others

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing the sharing of their visual artwork, such as in a display in the classroom or school corridor or shared with the class as a reflection and feedback opportunity (such as at a school assembly or sent home to families)

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to express ideas about work they have created with another person

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attending to their artworks being shown in a digital presentation, for example by using sounds, gestures or movements when an image of their artwork is displayed on a screen

elaborations.name: VC2AFAP01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a review of a presentation of class artworks and indicating their feelings about the artworks, for example by using sounds, gestures or movements to indicate their preferences for artwork features such as subject, elements and emotions

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Media Arts - Foundation Level B (The Arts FLA-FLD)

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation Level B, the Arts builds on students’ prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for sensory exploration and experiential approaches that enable arts learning experiences across the 5 Arts disciplines: Dance, Drama, Music, Media Arts and Visual Arts. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline.

In Foundation Level B, students explore, develop practices and contribute to creating through the Arts disciplines by participating and engaging in arts experiences, elements, forms, materials and/or technologies.

Learning in the Arts involves exploring ideas in arts works from different people and communities, within structured learning opportunities appropriate for the learning needs of individual students.

Students contribute to the co-creation of group arts works in response to a shared experience or observation.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Foundation Level B, students engage with arts works they encounter at school, home and in the community.

They participate in the co-creation of arts works that explore ideas and they identify their contribution to the presentation of arts works to others.

Dance

Students engage with the elements of dance to develop personal movement.

Drama

Students engage with the elements of drama and expressive skills to develop characters, situations and/or settings.

Media Arts

Students engage with media arts forms, language and/or technologies.

Music

Students engage with the elements of music and instruments to develop sounds.

Visual Arts

Students engage with art elements and materials.

elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.elaboration_text: attempting to imitate familiar actions when moving or dancing to a favourite or familiar song or piece of music

elaborations.elaboration_text: learning and practising fundamental movements to develop balance and coordination

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: physically interpreting different genres in music, for example by moving their body, an instrument or prop in response to different beats

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: moving in response to rhythms played on an instrument, for example with small movements using their fingers or with large movements using their arms or body

elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring voices, movements and spaces in structured drama sessions

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: manipulating objects, puppets, two-dimensional images and available technologies to create stories

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using objects to represent another object, for example using a hat as a steering wheel

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: portraying characters by using simple actions

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and using a camera or other photographic device

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting images that represent an object or place and arranging images to represent an idea or story

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: improvising movements to communicate ideas and then having them filmed to be presented to others

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with images, for example by assisting to capture images using a digital device to represent the activities in a day, then selecting and arranging the images to retell the events of the day

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: anticipating changes in familiar music, for example by showing recognition when music is going to get louder, quieter or stop

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: controlling their musical choices, for example by selecting songs from an electronic resource or picture card or by selecting and exploring an instrument for a short period of time

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: attempting to move, sing or engage in actions associated with chants or songs, for example using their preferred communication modality to contribute to a favourite song in a group singing activity

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in music-making activities

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning how to hold and use instruments to create sounds or vibrations

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring arts tools through sensory art experiences, for example briefly holding and using familiar tools such as a paintbrush, roller or sponge or attempting to use a tool after its use has been demonstrated

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the use of colour and materials before and during the creation of a visual arts work or design

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E25 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring arts materials and mediums through sensory art experiences, for example by using wet and dry materials, clay, modelling dough, printmaking techniques, paper, cardboard, cloth and other natural materials to create a group collage, sculpture, mural or installation

elaborations.name: VC2AFBD01-E26 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting with a variety of mediums, materials, textures and techniques associated with artworks

content_descriptions.name: VC2AFBC01 - The Arts
content_descriptions.text: co-construct arts works in response to stimulus

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E01 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the co-creation of a group dance by selecting a movement, prop, material or piece of music

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E03 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to share an idea to include in a dance from a recent experience, for example suggesting the idea of an animal movement after watching a documentary about animals

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E04 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an awareness of others when developing a dance work, for example attending to the movement of others or changing position to provide space for others

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing an awareness of how objects, people, sounds, movements and changes in lighting can be used to represent or signify something else, such as the lights being dimmed to suggest nightfall or a character wearing a hat, scarf and gloves to indicate cold weather

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to a change in atmosphere by responding to a cue or signal such as someone tiptoeing quietly past a sleeping giant played by a student in-role or a drum roll announcing the arrival of the king

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using characters, dolls or figurines to play out simple actions

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E09 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the use of technologies to capture images or sounds, for example by using a switch or button to activate media equipment or by tapping a switch to capture an image or record a sound

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with images, for example by assisting to capture images with a camera or other device of an experience or learning activity then assisting to select and arrange images to retell a story of a school day

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring composition by selecting and ordering images and/or sounds to assist in the creation of a media arts work or represent preferred stories or songs

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in the development of an artwork by selecting images and/or sounds

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to create a variety of sounds and unstructured rhythms, which are recorded and then played back

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing an instrument and following a rhythm or pattern to include in a group music piece

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using percussive instruments with increasing confidence and skill to accompany tunes, songs or chants

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting sounds from a variety of sources to create simple sound ideas, individually and in groups

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: making drawings that indicate an emerging awareness of symbolic representation

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: making visual arts works in response to inspiration from sources such as play, imagination and observation

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating an artwork such as a painting or collage by identifying the colours and materials they want through choice making such as pointing, reaching or communicating what they want to use, for example selecting a colour from 2 or 3 options and adding these with assistance to their artwork

elaborations.name: VC2AFBC01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: making artworks in structured activities, for example creating a painting, sculpture or photograph of themselves

elaborations.elaboration_text: Dance

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E02 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: dancing to a favourite song or piece of music or having it recorded or photographed and then recognising the image

elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to a cue to perform a familiar action or dance as a group to peers, teachers or parents

elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying movements, props, sound/music or costumes they have used in a dance work

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E05 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing the sharing and presentation of their dance in a digital format

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E06 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E07 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating an interest in the effect of their actions on materials and resources

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E08 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: following cues to link an action to a story in their drama work

elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising themselves in a recording of a drama work

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E10 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying actions, props, sounds or costumes they have used in a drama work

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E11 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: rehearsing or practising actions or a sequence of actions to communicate an idea through drama

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E12 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying their contribution to aspects of a story that has been created by the class, for example by reacting to images or text that they have created

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying images or sounds that they have created in a moving animation based on a personal story or documentation of an event

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting images to accompany a story or experience that has been documented, for example choosing an image to accompany their experiences of a school excursion or their experiences of watching an animation or film

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E16 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: contributing to a class presentation reflecting on the year at school for the school assembly or newsletter

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to a prompt to play an instrument

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying their instrument in a group music work, either through rehearsal or an audio or visual recording of the music work

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to recordings of their performance, for example using their preferred communication modality to show recognition of their contribution to the performance

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to identify their visual artwork in a school exhibition and react to the work

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting an artwork or materials to contribute to a combined class installation on a topic or a response to a story or song

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating an artwork in response to a visit to an art exhibition or local sculpture walk

elaborations.name: VC2AFBP01-E25 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to select an artwork and make a short statement about the work to contribute to a class book of artworks or works based on a theme

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Media Arts - Foundation Level C (The Arts FLA-FLD)

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation Level C, the Arts builds on students’ prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for the design of structured experiences for students to engage in sensory exploration and the practical application of arts approaches that enable learning experiences across the 5 Arts disciplines: Dance, Drama, Music, Media Arts and Visual Arts. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline.

In Foundation Level C, students explore ideas communicated through the arts works of different people and communities. 

Learning in the Arts involves students developing practices in the disciplines and communicating ideas through the use of art elements, forms, materials, technologies or techniques.

Students create and share their arts works in informal settings such as the classroom.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Foundation Level C, students respond to arts works they encounter at school, home and in the community.

They create arts works and present these to others.

Dance

Students explore the elements of dance and production elements to develop dance works.

They use their bodies, objects and/or materials when responding to personal experiences to create dance works.

Drama

Students explore stories and the elements of drama, expressive skills and production areas to develop drama works.

They use elements of drama, expressive skills and production areas when responding to personal experiences to create drama works.

Media Arts

Students explore media arts forms, language and technologies to construct media arts works.

They use media languages, processes and technologies when responding to personal experiences to create media arts works.

Music

Students explore sound sources, instruments and elements of music to develop music works.

They use elements of music and instruments when responding to personal experiences to create music works.

Visual Arts

Students explore art elements, materials and techniques.

They use art elements, materials and techniques when responding to personal experiences to create visual arts works.

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Media Arts - Foundation Level D (The Arts FLA-FLD)

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation Level D, the Arts builds on students’ prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for the design of structured experiences for students to engage in sensory exploration and the practical application of arts approaches that enable learning experiences across the 5 Arts disciplines: Dance, Drama, Music, Media Arts and Visual Arts. There are examples in the elaborations for each discipline.

In Foundation Level D, students explore how ideas are represented in a variety of ways by different people and communities.

Learning in the Arts involves students developing practices in the disciplines and communicating ideas by experimenting with different art elements, forms, materials, technologies or techniques.

Students share meaning through their creation of arts works and share their arts works with familiar people.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Foundation Level D, students respond to stories, observations and ideas about arts works they encounter at school, home and in the community.

They create, share and present arts works with others.

Dance

Students explore the elements of dance and production elements to develop dance works that represent ideas.

They use movement and elements of dance to communicate ideas in dance works.

Drama

Students explore the elements of drama, expressive skills and production elements to develop drama works that represent ideas.

They use elements of drama, expressive skills and production areas to represent characters and settings to communicate ideas in drama works.

Media Arts

Students use media languages, processes and technologies to construct media arts works and to represent ideas and stories.

They develop and present media arts works that represent ideas and stories to audiences.

Music

Students explore sound sources, elements of music and instruments to develop music works that represent ideas.

They use elements of music and instruments to communicate ideas and meaning in music works.

Visual Arts

Students respond to ideas in visual arts works and explore art elements, materials, techniques and processes to develop arts works that express ideas in different arts forms.

They use art elements, materials, techniques and processes to communicate their ideas in arts works in different arts forms.

elaborations.elaboration_text: Media Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E13 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: displaying and discussing their media arts works with others

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E14 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a visual and/or audio story or a poster using graphics software with the intention to meet an audience need, for example by retelling a familiar story using a combination of images, symbols or sounds or a poster that recounts an event to share with the class

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E15 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing class experiences and presenting them in the form of a class photo story or using PowerPoint

elaborations.elaboration_text: assisting in the production and presentation of an artwork for a particular purpose, for example helping to create a poster about expectations when using cameras in the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E17 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Music

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E18 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing music in a way that shows emerging music knowledge and skills, for example by performing music at a celebration that demonstrates elements of music such as rhythm

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E19 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating music to communicate ideas, concepts, observations, feelings and/or experiences, for example by choosing and combining sounds to create compositions for presentation

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E20 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: employing patterns of body movement such as clapping or stamping and performing accompaniments to familiar music

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E21 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting using music technologies such as digital audio workstation software

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E22 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating appropriate audience behaviour when in the classroom and when attending school functions, for example by watching for an extended period of time and responding to performance, clapping at the conclusion and identifying strategies that will help them with this (such as cues and images)

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E23 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: Visual Arts

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E24 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to discuss features of their own and others’ visual arts works using a few short spoken or written sentences, for example expressing the features they like best in their own artwork, identifying the main materials used in artworks or describing some of the characteristics of their artwork

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E25 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using their preferred communication modality to discuss ideas such as themes in relation to the display of artworks, such as at the local gallery or in their classroom

elaborations.elaboration_text: deciding which of their artworks to display and how to display them

elaborations.name: VC2AFDP01-E27 – The Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experiencing and identifying the roles of artist and audience

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Foundation, learning in Media Arts builds on the Victorian Early Years Learning and Development Framework (VEYLDF) and each student’s prior learning and experiences. The curriculum allows for experimental approaches that integrate arts learning experiences across the different Arts disciplines and/or specialist teaching. There are examples in the elaborations for each content description and examples that span across the disciplines.

In Foundation, learning fosters students’ understanding of how media arts enrich their lives and the lives of all people. Engagement with media arts strengthens students’ sense of wellbeing and develops their connections with the world. Learning in Media Arts involves exploration and purposeful, creative play, together with structured learning appropriate for students' level of development. In Media Arts, students work individually and collaboratively with peers and teachers, drawing on their imaginations, stimulus materials such as images or works of fiction, and real-life experiences.

In Foundation, the focus is on students:

  • exploring and responding to media arts works across cultures, and in their lives and communities, including the media arts works and practices of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples
  • developing media arts practices through structured play, experimentation, imagination and inquiry
  • creating media arts works using technologies, materials and equipment to make artworks that represent their ideas about the world
  • presenting and sharing their media arts works.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Foundation, students describe experiences, observations, ideas and feelings about media arts works they encounter at school, home and in the community. Students develop an understanding of media arts processes. They use play, imagination and experimentation with media arts processes to create media arts works. Students make and share media arts works to communicate their experiences and ideas.

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS1
organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS3
organising_ideas.text: Economic, social, environmental and cultural systems influence the sustainability of Earth’s systems.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSWV1
organising_ideas.text: Worldviews influence local and global action and, therefore, impact the interdependence of Earth’s systems. Worldviews can play a crucial role in achieving sustainability.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSWV2
organising_ideas.text: Worldviews are formed by different experiences at a personal, local, national and global level, and are linked to individual, community and political mandates and actions for sustainability.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSWV3
organising_ideas.text: Worldviews that are based on, but not limited to, the 4 pillars of sustainable development consider the intergenerational impact of current and future actions.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSRD1
organising_ideas.text: Responsibly designed products and services aim to minimise the human impact on the environment and restore the quality, ecological integrity and diversity of economic, social, environmental and cultural systems.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSRD2
organising_ideas.text: Responsible design considers unexpected consequences that might impact individuals, communities and ecological integrity in the future. Creative, empathetic and innovative design is integral to the achievement of sustainable living.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSRD3
organising_ideas.text: Responsible design requires a recognition and appreciation of land custodianship, past practices, contemporary research and technological advancements, and balanced and informed decisions based on understanding possible interconnected economic, social, environmental and cultural impacts.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSFT1
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable futures thinking is based on informed views that consider possible and desirable futures. It leads to individual, community, organisational and political action that reduces risk.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSFT2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable futures thinking creates desirable futures that value local, community, national and global equity and fairness across generations and into the future.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSFT3
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable futures thinking requires individuals to think creatively, seek information, identify a variety of possibilities, reflect and evaluate actions, and collaborate with and influence others as they work towards desired futures.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 1 and 2, learning in the Arts builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences. Students continue to learn through purposeful and creative play in structured learning programs designed to foster a strong sense of wellbeing and develop their connection with and contribution to the world. They work individually and in collaboration with peers and teachers, drawing on their imaginations, works of fiction, real-life experiences and learnings from across the curriculum to support their engagement in Arts learning, as artists and as audiences.

Students explore media arts works that they experience at home, at school or through family and community events. They connect with media artists who live and work in the community, for example by visiting arts spaces or exploring media arts works and experiences such as in-person or online screenings, exhibitions or presentations. They use stimulus materials such as images, events, texts, questions and observations as inspiration for their own media arts works. These experiences support students to develop aesthetic knowledge across cognitive, sensory, emotive and physical domains, and to value media arts works and practices from across cultures, communities and/or other contexts.

In Levels 1 and 2, the focus is on students:

  • exploring and responding to media arts works and media arts practices they experience across cultures, times, places and other contexts, including media arts works created by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples
  • developing creative practices for using media languages and available technologies
  • developing critical practices for observing, reflecting on and responding to their own media arts works and those they experience
  • creating media arts works by selecting and combining images, sounds, text and/or interactive elements
  • presenting or sharing media arts works they have created in informal settings.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body: By the end of Level 2, students identify where they experience media arts. They describe where, when, why and how people across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts experience media arts. Students experiment with media production processes. They use media arts languages and technologies to construct representations in media arts works. Students share their work with audiences in informal settings.

organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures- VC2CCPACP2
organising_ideas.text: The occupation and colonisation of the land now known as Australia by the British, under the now overturned doctrine of terra nullius, were experienced by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples as an invasion that denied their occupancy of, and connection to, Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples are the Traditional Owners of Country and Place, protected in Australian law by the Native Title Act 1993, which recognises pre-existing sovereignty, continuing systems of law and customs, and connection to Country and Place.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC3
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people belong to the world’s oldest continuous cultures. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples demonstrate resilience in the maintenance, practice and revitalisation of culture despite the many historic and enduring impacts of colonisation, and they continue to celebrate and share the past, present and future manifestations of their cultures.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

content_descriptions.name: VC2AMA2D01 - Media Arts
content_descriptions.text: explore ways of using media technologies to capture and organise images, sounds, text and/or interactive elements

elaborations.name: VC2AMA2D01-E01 - Media Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using viewpoints to develop questions as they experiment with media technologies, such as ‘What happens if I take a photo close to the object and how does it change as I move further away?’ and ‘How can I change the meaning of this image by adding different text headings?’

elaborations.name: VC2AMA2D01-E02 - Media Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring ways to use digital tools to capture moving images; for example, using a digital device to capture and manipulate short videos, or adding sound effects or voice overs to communicate ideas or a narrative

elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with images; for example, retelling the story of a school day using a digital camera to capture still or moving images and adding appropriate captions

elaborations.name: VC2AMA2D01-E04 - Media Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with ways that media artists communicate with audiences by combining text, symbols and images

content_descriptions.name: VC2AMA2C01 - Media Arts
content_descriptions.text: use media languages and media technologies to construct representations

elaborations.name: VC2AMA2C01-E01 - Media Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using viewpoints to develop questions when making decisions about the construction of a media narrative, for example asking questions about the use of elements and content, such as ‘What images will I keep or delete?’ and ‘Which image interests me and why?’

elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting and editing images, sound and text to recreate the characters in well-known stories or songs

elaborations.elaboration_text: capturing and sequencing images and text to create a media arts work, such as a comic book that retells familiar or traditional stories

elaborations.elaboration_text: producing and presenting a media arts work for a particular purpose; for example, creating an advertisement that recommends appropriate behaviour when using cameras

elaborations.name: VC2AMA2C01-E05 - Media Arts
elaborations.elaboration_text: using features such as shot types in media arts works, for example identifying long shots, medium shots and close-ups, and discussing what the shots tell the audience about the story

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 3 and 4, learning in Media Arts builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences. Learning in Media Arts in Levels 3 and 4 continues to use purposeful and creative play-based activities that foster the development of students’ identity and wellbeing, and their connection with and contribution to the world. Students further develop their capability and confidence in using discipline-specific skills, and creative and critical practices. They work individually and in collaboration with peers and teachers.

Students continue to explore media arts works that they experience at home, at school or through family and community events. They connect with media artists who live and work in the community, for example by visiting arts spaces or exploring media arts and experiences such as in-person or online screenings, exhibitions and presentations. They use stimulus materials such as images, events, texts, questions and observations as inspiration for their own media arts works. These experiences support students to develop aesthetic knowledge across cognitive, sensory, emotive and physical domains, and to value artworks and practices from across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts such as countries or cultures in Asia.

In Levels 3 and 4, the focus is on students:

  • exploring and responding to media arts works and experiences that showcase where, when, why and how media is created and used across cultures, times, places and other contexts
  • exploring and responding to media arts works created by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples that communicate connection to and responsibility for Country and Place
  • developing creative practices for using media arts concepts, and visual, audio and/or interactive elements
  • developing critical practices for observing, reflecting on and responding to media they experience, including their own media arts works
  • creating and producing media arts works in a range of forms to communicate ideas to audiences using media technologies and media languages
  • presenting media arts works they have created in informal settings such as spaces within the school.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 4, students identify and describe the media languages and media technologies used to construct representations in media arts works they experience and/or produce. They recall where, when, why and how media arts works are created and distributed across cultures, times, places and other contexts, including the work of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples.

Students explore and experiment with media arts production processes and technologies. They use media languages, technologies and production processes to communicate ideas, perspectives and meaning in media arts works. Students share their work in informal and formal settings with different audiences using responsible media practice.

organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
